prompt:
Flat design render of a webpage UI (not a photograph, not a poster). The webpage is "Simon's Hangman", a hangman word game, captured mid-round at desktop size 1440x1000.

WORLD: The whole viewport is one sheet of warm cream sketchbook paper (#f4efe4) with a faint pencil-tooth grain. Every element is drawn in soft graphite pencil strokes with slightly wobbly, hand-drawn linework. No straight digital edges, no gloss, no drop-shadow UI cards, no color except one muted red pencil accent (#c0392b) reserved for wrong-guess marks. Graphite shades range from light HB gray to dark 6B.

STRUCTURE: The page is an open sketchbook spread: a soft vertical gutter shadow in the middle divides the sheet into two pages, and a faint spiral binding sketch runs along the gutter. 

LEFT PAGE (about 45% of the width): a large hand-drawn hangman drawing dominates it — gallows base, vertical post, top beam and rope are complete in firm graphite; the stick figure has head, body and one arm sketched in darker 6B strokes; light construction guide lines and eraser smudge trails are visible around the figure. Three small red pencil tally hatch marks sit in the bottom corner of this page. A small handwritten graphite title "Simon's Hangman" sits at the top of the left page.

RIGHT PAGE (about 55%): centered large handwritten secret word with eight letter slots: "E _ _ P H _ N T" — the letters E, L, P, H, N, T written in firm graphite, the three unknown slots shown as hand-drawn underline dashes. Below the word, one short handwritten status line: "3 wrong guesses". Below that, an A-to-Z letter grid in four rows of seven: each letter hand-written above its own pencil underline. Letters E, L, P, H, N, T are filled in darker; letters R, S, O each crossed out with one red pencil stroke and dimmed; all remaining letters in soft graphite. In the bottom right corner, a small hand-drawn rounded-rectangle button reads "New word".

No browser chrome, no navigation bar, no footer, no logos. The visitor's job — guess letters to reveal the word before the drawing completes — must be readable from the image alone.
